title: Polydatin inhibits hippocampal neurodegeneration in diabetic rats via modulation of oxidative stress and NF-kB/COX-2/IL-6 inflammatory pathway.
authors: Yousef, Ahmed I; El-Twab, Sanaa M Abd; Khadrawy, Sally M; Abdel-Moneim, Adel; Khalil, Rehab G
one_liner_zh: 该文研究虎杖苷对糖尿病大鼠海马神经变性的保护作用，分子对接仅针对BACE1和AChE酶，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Impaired insulin function and persistent hyperglycemia damage the brain of diabetics and raise the risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although polydatin (PLD) possesses promising biological effects, no major study has yet explored its anti-neurodegenerative efficacy in the hippocampus. This study therefore aims to investigate the probable protective effects of PLD against hippocampal neurodegeneration in diabetic rats, as well as explore its in-silico inhibitory activity against two key enzymes implicated in the progression of AD. Experimental diabetes was induced in male albino rats then PLD was administered orally to the diabetic rats (50 mg/kg b.wt.) daily for four weeks. In silico molecular docking was used to predict the interactions of PLD against BACE1 and AChE. PLD treatment significantly improved diabetic parameters, lowering blood glucose and raising serum insulin. Excitingly, PLD markedly alleviated oxidative stress by reducing lipid peroxidation and nitric oxide levels while enhancing antioxidant defenses (elevated GPx activity and GSH content) in the hippocampus of diabetic rats. PLD also suppressed neuroinflammation by down-regulating NF-kappaB, COX-2, and IL-6 mRNA expression. Furthermore, PLD significantly elevated the protein level of IDE while lowered Abeta(1-42) level. In silico, PLD revealed potent binding affinity for BACE1 (-8.6 Kcal/mol) and AChE (-10.5 Kcal/mol), interacting with key residues, indicating its inhibition potential. Overall, PLD effectively reduced neurodegeneration in the hippocampus of diabetic rats via inhibiting oxidative stress, inflammation, and Abeta(1-42) accumulation. PLD may act as a promising multi-target anti-neurodegenerative candidate, capable of simultaneously modulating multiple pathways and more experimental validation are needed in the future.
abstract_zh: 胰岛素功能受损和持续性高血糖会损害糖尿病患者的脑部，并增加阿尔茨海默病（AD）的风险。尽管虎杖苷（PLD）具有前景广阔的生物学效应，但尚无重大研究探讨其在海马体中的抗神经退行性功效。因此，本研究旨在探讨PLD对糖尿病大鼠海马神经退行性变的潜在保护作用，并探索其对AD进展中涉及的两个关键酶的计算机模拟抑制活性。实验性糖尿病在雄性白化大鼠中诱导，随后糖尿病大鼠每日口服PLD（50 mg/kg体重），持续四周。采用计算机模拟分子对接预测PLD与BACE1和AChE的相互作用。PLD治疗显著改善了糖尿病参数，降低了血糖并提高了血清胰岛素水平。令人兴奋的是，PLD通过降低脂质过氧化和一氧化氮水平，同时增强抗氧化防御（提高GPx活性和GSH含量），显著减轻了糖尿病大鼠海马中的氧化应激。PLD还通过下调NF-kappaB、COX-2和IL-6 mRNA表达抑制了神经炎症。此外，PLD显著提高了IDE蛋白水平，同时降低了Abeta(1-42)水平。在计算机模拟中，PLD对BACE1（-8.6 Kcal/mol）和AChE（-10.5 Kcal/mol）显示出强效结合亲和力，与关键残基相互作用，表明其抑制潜力。总体而言，PLD通过抑制氧化应激、炎症和Abeta(1-42)积累，有效减轻了糖尿病大鼠海马中的神经退行性变。PLD可能作为有前景的多靶点抗神经退行性候选药物，能够同时调节多条通路，未来需要更多实验验证。
